body: Experience the iconic Lotus Tower, the tallest structure in Sri Lanka, standing proudly in the heart of Colombo. Soaring 350 meters into the sky, this architectural marvel resembles a blooming lotus and offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city, Beira Lake, and the surrounding landscapes. Visitors can explore its observation deck, enjoy fine dining at the tower’s revolving restaurant, and capture unforgettable photos of Colombo’s skyline. Whether you’re a first-time traveler or a seasoned explorer, Lotus Tower is a must-visit attraction, combining modern engineering with cultural symbolism, making it a highlight of any Sri Lankan adventure.

body: Those interested in Buddhism know very well that the lotus is a pretty aquatic color with large yellow or pink petals - in this religion is not just a beautiful plant. The lotus symbolizes primordial waters, spiritual opening, wisdom and nirvana. Personally, I was quite surprised to learn that the lotus is not dedicated to anyone there, but to the Buddha himself!!! It is an image of purity and perfection: growing out of mud, it always remains pure. Likewise, beings born in one world of sansars but sincerely practicing the teachings of the Buddha are able to rid themselves of the shadows over time. And so I was not at all surprised to learn that one of the main must-sees of Sri Lanka's capitals is called the Colombo Lotus Tower. All because the design of this majestic structure was inspired by the lotus flower. You can easily find it in almost the centre of Colombo, on the promenade of Lake Beira. It is there that the 356-meter-long "stroyhouse" - the Tower "Lotus" - stands (the height is given taking into account the spire at the top, although many sources indicate the entire height of 350 meters). “Nelum Kuluna” and “Taamaray Kopuram” – so melodious and mysterious to our ears are its names in Sinhala and Tamil respectively. This structure cannot be confused with any other - if only because this Tower is the second tallest in South Asia. And the 19th place (again in height) among the towers of the world is also impressive!!! Its construction began in January 2012 and was completed in September seven years later. Alas, I have not been able to find information about the author of the construction project in any source. It's probably the product of collective creativity. Only in one place did I find mention that students from the Department of Architecture at the University of Moratuwa in Sri Lanka participated in the design of the Tower. I don't vouch for the veracity of the information, however. The Lotus Tower’s “petals” are illuminated by colourful LED lights at night and the barrel shines a spotlight, which, in my humble opinion, makes the site particularly beautiful precisely at night. The Lotus Tower is certainly a must-visit site in Colombo. I recommend it!!!
title: . Colombo Lotus Tower: Spiritual Revelation, Wisdom and Nirvana in the Image of a TV Tower

body: This Review is solely for the Blue Orbit Citrus Restaurant. Make Reservations directly with the Restaurant, the Buffet is roughly 20-30 dollars per adult, where I found some third party apps charging close to 60 USD per adult! Making a reservation was a little hard to understand, but a text and a call and a little faith that they saved your reservation and you are in there, they give a window, and not a specific time which took me a second to pick up on. When you arrive, dont be intimidated if there is a wrap around line outside, that line is for the observation deck. Just inform an attendant that you made a reservation and they will walk you directly to the elevator (making you feel a little bad for skipping the line, but also like a badass VIP) The windows closest to the windows are for couples only and do not rotate, but there is a rotating platform for the rest of the tables that my kids enjoyed. The view is amazing, we went at night so the lights were pretty, but I bet seeing it in the day is also great. The food was good, a mix of Sri Lankan, Indian and Chinese all in one Buffet.

Great to have this for locals as the only viewing tower in the country. However, there was nothing else of interest there. body: Colombo Lotus TowerThe Colombo Lotus Tower, standing proudly in the heart of Colombo, is South Asia’s tallest self-supported structure and Sri Lanka’s tallest skyscraper, reaching an impressive height of 356 meters (1168 feet). Designed to resemble a lotus blossom, a symbol of purity and renewal, this iconic structure reflects the blend of tradition and modernity in Sri Lanka. With construction initiated in 2012, the tower was meticulously crafted over a decade and opened to the public on 15th September 2022, marking a new chapter in Sri Lanka’s architectural and technological advancement.Situated along the banks of Beira Lake, the Colombo Lotus Tower is a landmark visible from far beyond the city limits, drawing thousands of visitors each month who come to experience its panoramic observation deck, cutting-edge technology, and entertainment facilities. The tower offers a 360-degree view of Colombo, the Indian Ocean, and the lush landscapes that extend inland, making it a prime spot for sightseeing, photography, and cultural immersion.

body: Sri Lanka still employs a two-tier pricing system, which many tourists find frustrating. For instance, I recently observed 20–30 foreigners choosing not to pay the higher rates, while just as many expressed dissatisfaction on their way out. It raises the question: is this approach sustainable in today’s global tourism market? I had walked from Galle Face and decided to rest, but the experience left me reflecting on how this outdated pricing system affects Sri Lanka's appeal. Tourists increasingly share their experiences online, and negative feedback can deter potential visitors. As tourism evolves, Sri Lanka should consider modernizing its policies. A fair pricing system could significantly enhance the visitor experience, encouraging return visits and bolstering the country's reputation. Hopefully, as new generations step into leadership, they'll prioritize more inclusive and progressive approaches to tourism that benefit both visitors and the local economy. The price for this attraction is far too high and certainly not worth the money or a pleasant experience.
reviewer_location: Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
title: Two tier system and not worth the money

body: After looking at this beautiful building spectacle from our hotel room for several days and finding out it has a revolving restaurant, we decided to make the visit.. Firstly we were over charged by a Tuk Tuk driver for a 400 lkr journey where the driver tried to charge us 5000lkr. Upon arriving at the Lotus Tower we entered the queue and paid a fee of 11574lkr to get tickets to enter. This is 20$ us each for 2. We entered the building through an airport style security bag scan and then got in a queue for the lifts. Whilst presenting our tickets we asked if this was the way to the restaurant bar to which the answer was yes and our ticket stubs were torn so we proceeded with all the other guests to the lifts which took us directly to the top floor viewing point. Not knowing where the bar actually was we walked around looking for the bar restaurant to be told we had to go back to reception and then book on the 1st floor. We ventured back down to the ground floor and asked the staff about the restaurant and we were told the ticket wasn't needed for entry to the restaurant and that it was for the digital art experience on the ground floor and viewing point only. By this point we were 20 mins in which is how long it took to get to the top and bottom again without stopping including queues. After explaining that we didn't realise we didn't need a ticket to A enter the building as this is far from obvious to a foreign traveller and B we certainly wouldn't have purchased a ticket for a digital exhibition we had no interest in seeing. No we're a little confused so we asked for help and explained we don't want the exhibition or viewing point as there's plenty to be seen from a revolving restaurant anyway. The staff then laughed at us for being stupid foreigners who made a mistake and actually smiled the upset we got for buying something we don't use or need, further they weren't prepared to offer a refund and allow us to spend the money in the restaurant as it's apparently a separate business to the tower attractions. Standing in the lobby trying to explain our mistake made no difference to the staff and no matter who we spoke to on this subject we were treated with total disrespect and laughter at our mistake only to be told it's company policy not to offer refunds. Like we are trying to take something from them. We both found it rude and inconsiderate. We've spent plenty of money in Sri Lanka since visiting and tipped well everyone we visit. Sri Lanka as a whole we've found completely amazing. However 2 days from the end of our trip to be insulated and worse laughed at for an honest mistake was awful. Sadly we left not only without using the tickets or visiting the restaurant bar. What's more sad is that we couldn't even give the tickets to another couple outside as the first thing they do when you get in is tear the stub. Terrible experience, awful attitude from staff. Extremely disappointed.
title: Terrible Visit to Lotus Tower

title: Amazing 360 degree views
Recommended for the last day of your trip
body: Great 360° view of the city.The movies in the museum are for children but I could learn the history.Good place to check the direction I visited and reflect on my trip.When I visited, local elementary school students were visiting for a school event. It was very funny to see them all enjoying the scenery, and it made me happy as well.

title: Lotus Tower: Good
body: Great views of the city and Indian Ocean as you’d expect with brief information on the obs deck. There is an interactive element at ground level which does a good job of summarising Colombo’s history and tower location, if not a little touristy and gimmicky afterwards.

title: Must visit in Colombo
body: We visited the Lotus tower and it was great. Being the highest observation tower in South Asia and being on top 20 towers in the world, this is a must visit if you're in Colombo. The first thing you notice is the differential ticket pricing for tourists vs locals which is a typical Sri Lankan process. The tour all the way to the observation deck is well organised with a stopover at a display which shows some details about the tower. Then off to the elevator that takes you up to level 29 where the observation deck is. The day was very clear so we could see all the way down towards central Sri Lanka and all suburbs of Colombo. It also provides good views of port city currently under construction. Overall a highly recommended visit if you're in Colombo.

title: Symbolic landmark in Colombo
body: Lotus tower is a symbolic landmark in the city of Colombo. It has a height of more than 350 metres. This is the tallest tower in South Asia. There is an observation deck on the top which one can visit post buying a ticket of USD 20. Below the observation deck, the tower also has a beautiful revolving restaurant, however one has to pre-book the same. Would highly recommend a visit.

title: Lofty Lotus Tower
body: The Lotus Tower is more beautiful on the outside than on the inside. However, the observation deck offers 360-degree views of Colombo.
